summary: Umpqua National Forest L-4 ground cabin planned in a 1932 news item and built that year; a 1942 lookout ranger is reported, it was abandoned in 1965, and it is listed as gone.

facts.design: 14 x 14 L-4 ground cabin (no unit given in the source)
facts.status_note: firelookout.com and the Oregon lookout list both mark it gone; no source describes what remains

staffing.status: staffed in summer 1942 (one lookout ranger reported)

events.note: 14 x 14 L-4 ground cabin constructed; a July 1932 news item had planned one at Umpqua hot springs
Alan Knudtson, son of a local jeweler, reported as lookout ranger for the summer
firelookout.com gives 1965 as the abandonment year

evidence.supports: July 1932 news item: nine new lookout houses planned at an estimated cost of $5,300
evidence.quote: Nine new lookout houses are to be built at an estimated cost of $5,300.

evidence.supports: one of the planned lookouts was to be at Umpqua hot springs in the upper meadows district
evidence.quote: will be built at Umpqua hot springs in the upper meadows district.
1932: A 14 x 14 L-4 ground cabin constructed.

evidence.supports: 1942 Alan Knudtson, son of a local jeweler, lookout ranger for the summer
evidence.quote: A.M. Knudtson, local jeweler, is spending a week vacationing at the Hot Springs lookout ranger station visiting his son, Alan, who is lookout ranger there for the summer.

evidence.supports: the Forest Lookouts page ends with the bare label Removed, undated
Oregon lookout list: ground lookout, gone
evidence.quote: Umpqua Hot Spring Douglas 43.30207 -122.36368 Ground Gone

evidence.supports: the 1932 news item was printed in the Roseburg News-Review
1942 item dated July 28, 1942, in the same paper

sources.title: Umpqua Hot Spring Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: Coordinates conflict in the brief (FFLA 43.30207, -122.36368 vs west_us_lookouts 43.3053, -122.3466); the story gives none. Wikipedia's Umpqua Hot Springs article gives 43.295035, -122.365873 (not cited), about 0.8 km from the FFLA point. The bare 'Removed' label on the Forest Lookouts page has no date and its meaning is unclear, so the story quotes it only as written. Two WebSearch queries found no separate lookout record; Butler Butte and Red Butte on firelookout.com are other towers and were not used. Access and visit are left out because no source describes the site today.
